questions.prompt: How does your result tell the model which call it answers?

options.explanation: The same tool can be called more than once. Results are matched by id.

options.text: It carries the call's id: `tool_use_id` on Claude, `call_id` on OpenAI.
options.explanation: Right. Each result points to exactly one call.

options.text: It is matched by position: the first result answers the first call, and so on.
options.explanation: Both vendors use an id to match results to calls.

questions.prompt: Your tool hit a rate limit. On Claude, what do you send back?

options.text: A `tool_result` with `is_error: true` and a message like "Rate limit exceeded. Retry after 60 seconds."
options.explanation: Right. That is the Claude docs' own example of an instructive error.

options.text: Nothing. Stop the whole conversation and show the user a generic error page, then log the failure for later.
options.explanation: The Claude tutorial says to send the error back instead of crashing, so Claude can recover.

questions.prompt: A tool can return 5,000 records. What does the vendor guidance suggest?

options.text: Return all 5,000 records in full so the model never misses anything the user might ask about.
options.explanation: The Claude docs warn that bloated responses waste context.
A random sample may drop the record the user needs. Filter by what matters, then page.

options.text: Return only high-signal fields, with filters, paging or truncation.
options.explanation: Right. That is the advice in the Claude docs and Anthropic's tool guide.
A count alone gives the model nothing to answer with.
